text:
The Rangers arrived in Edmonton on a three-game winning streak and left without it, beaten 3-1 by a team that spent most of the night chasing the puck. The man who made the difference was Devon Levi, a goalie drafted 212th overall by the Panthers in 2020, who stopped 28 of 29 shots.

By our numbers, the Rangers were the better team by a wide margin. Their expected goals (the quality of chances, shot by shot) came to 3.6 against 1.96 for the Oilers, and in our simulated replays of every shot, NYR wins 85 percent of the time. They out-attempted Edmonton 60 to 40. Levi's goals saved above expected, which measures how many more goals a goalie stopped than the chances deserved, was 2.6. He turned away a 38 percent look from Noah Laba in the first period, and New York went 0 for 5 on the power play despite 1.36 expected goals with the man advantage.

Edmonton took the goals it was handed. Connor McDavid scored on a 4 percent chance in the first period, and Leon Draisaitl made it 2-0 early in the second. Jaroslav Chmelar cut it to 2-1 shorthanded, but Draisaitl's second, also shorthanded, came on a 53 percent chance with 13 seconds left and sealed it. Edmonton had won the first meeting 4-1 on Nov. 1, and the Rangers have now dropped both games this season. Their streak ends at three, and they'll wonder what it takes to beat a hot goalie.
